newsitem.title: UK: Labour unions slam UK do-it-yourself railway.
newsitem.headline: Labour unions slam UK do-it-yourself railway.

text.p: British trade union officials on Friday criticised a rail company's plans to pay commuters to act as guards and assistants.

Great Eastern Railway said it would offer free travel and pay 5.25 pounds ($8.79) an hour to travellers who are willing to make train announcements, check that doors are closed, give signals to drivers and help other passengers.
The private company's commercial director decided to launch the scheme, based on one he had seen in Hong Kong, after the firm failed to find enough part-time workers during a recruitment campaign.

"Most commuters prefer to relax, read the paper or sleep. Others use the journey as part of their working day, but there is no doubt this could be a lucrative way of spending the journey," Mike Turner told the Times newspaper.
So far only 40 people have applied for the 14 part-time jobs on the company's eastern route out of London and only three passed the required tests before a one-week training programme.
The commuter guards, who will be given uniforms, would have to work half an hour before and throughout the 90-minute journey.
Union leaders slammed the scheme as a cost-cutting measure and warned that it could be dangerous. Some commuters also feared that it was unsafe.

"A do-it-yourself railway is the most bizarre proposal I have come across in nearly 40 years of involvement in the industry. There is more to being a guard than waving a flag and blowing a whistle," said Jimmy Knapp, the head of the main RMT rail union.
Another union official described it as a "safety nightmare."
